I am a 38-year-old farmer in Quzhou County with 13 years of experience. My family has 5 mu of land, and some of my household members work off-farm in the county town or nearby cities, so I have to manage labor carefully. I have a well on my farm, which means I can irrigate when I need to without waiting for rain.

My wheat was sown last October with improved seeds. It is now mid-April and the wheat is at jointing stage. I already applied revival fertilizer and irrigation in March. For the rest of this wheat season, I will top-dress urea at jointing and irrigate two more times—once now at jointing and again during grain filling if the weather turns dry. I apply about 20 kg of nitrogen per mu total for wheat, along with 8 kg phosphorus and 5 kg potassium as basal fertilizer. I will spray herbicide and fungicide twice in total. I expect about 550 kg per mu from the wheat if the weather holds.

After harvesting wheat in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize. Time is tight in our double-cropping system, and with limited family labor, I use no-tillage sowing to save two to three days and reduce fuel costs. I hire a service for this. For maize, I apply 18 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice—at sowing if the soil is dry after wheat harvest, and definitely at the big trumpet/tasseling stage. I spray herbicide once after emergence and insecticide for corn borer once if I see pests. I expect about 650 kg per mu from the maize.

I use improved wheat seeds and hybrid maize seeds because they give the best yield for my investment. I do not apply excessive fertilizer because costs have risen, and I have learned from 13 years of farming that balanced application gives me the best net return.
